```{python}
# | echo: false
import jammi_cookbook
```

**Recipe:** `fine_tune(method="lora", task=...)` on `[gpu]` against REAL checkpoints
· `infer` · `describe_model` — the SAME shipped Python surface the
`image_search`/`audio_search` recipes drive, never the internal `jammi-bench`
harness · **Theory:** LoRA — a frozen base weight plus a trainable low-rank update
[@hu2022lora] — injected into OpenCLIP's shared vision/text `ResidualAttentionBlock`
[@radford2021clip] and into CLAP's HTSAT-Swin audio tower [@wu2023clap] · **Rail:**
measurement (a real GPU fine-tune of each of three towers, its four invariants read
back through the public surface, frozen once and reasserted here).

Every earlier fine-tuning chapter in this book trains a **text** encoder
(ModernBERT). This one is the media front end's own proof: the SAME `fine_tune`
verb, pointed at REAL OpenCLIP ViT-B-32 (vision **and** text towers — `task=`
alone selects which) and REAL CLAP HTSAT (the audio tower) checkpoints, on real
GPU hardware, exercising the `target_modules` LoRA-site selectors the
`image_search`/`audio_search` recipes (PR #466) introduced for these
architectures. The heavy work — three LoRA fine-tunes plus their probes — ran
**once**, on a GPU `jammi-server`; this chapter reads that committed cache and
asserts a measured verdict against `golden_metrics.json`, never recomputing
upstream.

## Four things worth measuring, not one

A recipe that shows "the tuned vector differs from the base vector" is teaching
one fact. This chapter measures four, because each closes a gap the others leave
open:

1. **Change, not improvement.** The adapter must move the served embedding.
   Direction and quality are not claimed — a synthetic, generic triplet corpus
   carries no semantic ground truth — only that training changed something real.
2. **The same-input control.** A change could, in principle, be inference
   noise rather than a real parameter delta. The control rules that out: the
   SAME probe input, run through the SAME (base) checkpoint **twice**, in two
   independent calls. If this were nonzero, the "change" measurement above
   would be uninterpretable.
3. **The round trip.** A LoRA delta that trains but is silently dropped at
   serve time is the exact defect the recipes' own comments warn about. This
   chapter closes the connection that trained the adapter and opens a **new**
   one to the same server before re-deriving the tuned vector — proving the
   adapter survived into the catalog, not merely a training session's live
   state.
4. **The corrupt-row contract.** `generate-image-embeddings.md`'s documented
   claim is that a corrupt image is a per-row `_status="error"` outcome. This
   chapter measures what the branch actually does, on both image and audio
   media — see the finding below.

```{python}
from jammi_cookbook import contracts

record = contracts.load_artifact("media_tower.record")
print(f"engine version: {record['engine_version']}")
print(f"vision/text checkpoint: {record['vision_checkpoint']}")
print(f"audio checkpoint:       {record['audio_checkpoint']}")
print(f"rows per modality: {record['rows_per_modality']}")
```

## The three towers, measured side by side

`task=` is the only thing that changes which tower of the SAME OpenCLIP
checkpoint gets adapted (`image_embedding` -> vision, `text_embedding` -> the
CLIP text tower); the CLAP checkpoint carries a separate `audio_embedding`
tower. Every tower's `target_modules` names REAL sites on that tower's own
architecture (`in_proj`/`c_fc` on OpenCLIP's shared attention block;
`query`/`value`/`linear1` on HTSAT-Swin) — the same selector vocabulary the
`image_search`/`audio_search` recipes document.

```{python}
towers = record["towers"]
print(f"{'tower':<8}{'task':<18}{'target_modules'}")
for name, t in towers.items():
    print(f"{name:<8}{t['task']:<18}{t['target_modules']}")
```

### 1 — Change vs. base

Every tower's LoRA adapter measurably moved the served embedding on the SAME
probe input:

```{python}
for name, t in towers.items():
    diff = t["change_vs_base_max_abs_diff"]
    contracts.assert_close(f"media_tower.{name}.change_vs_base_max_abs_diff", diff)
    assert diff > 1e-4, (
        f"{name}: the LoRA adapter should change the served embedding — "
        f"max|Δ| = {diff:.6f} <= 1e-4 (adapter trained but not applied at serve time?)"
    )
    print(f"  {name:<6} change max|Δ| = {diff:.6f}  (> 1e-4 floor)")
```

### 2 — The same-input control

Two independent `infer` calls through the SAME (base) checkpoint, over the
SAME probe input. This is the control the "change" measurement above depends
on: a nonzero control diff would mean the change above could be
noise, not a real adapter effect.

```{python}
for name, t in towers.items():
    diff = t["same_input_control_max_abs_diff"]
    contracts.assert_close(f"media_tower.{name}.same_input_control_max_abs_diff", diff)
    print(f"  {name:<6} control max|Δ| = {diff:.6g}")

CONTROL_FLOOR = 1e-5  # far below every tower's own change-vs-base signal above
for name, t in towers.items():
    change = t["change_vs_base_max_abs_diff"]
    control = t["same_input_control_max_abs_diff"]
    assert control < CONTROL_FLOOR, (
        f"{name}: repeated inference through the SAME checkpoint over the SAME "
        f"input produced a non-negligible diff ({control:.6g}) — inference is "
        f"not deterministic here, and the change measurement above cannot be "
        f"trusted to reflect the adapter alone"
    )
    assert control < change, (
        f"{name}: the same-input control ({control:.6g}) is not smaller than "
        f"the change vs. base ({change:.6g}) — the measured change is not "
        f"distinguishable from noise"
    )
print("every tower's control diff is negligible AND strictly below its own "
      "change-vs-base signal ✓")
```

### 3 — The round trip: train → save → serve, from a NEW connection

After each job completes, the emit script closes the connection that trained
it and opens a **brand new** one to the same server before re-deriving the
tuned vector. A LoRA delta that trained but was dropped at serve time — the
exact defect the `image_search`/`audio_search` recipes' comments call out —
would show up here as either a `describe_model` miss or a vector that
disagrees with the first tuned read.

```{python}
for name, t in towers.items():
    diff = t["round_trip_max_abs_diff"]
    contracts.assert_close(f"media_tower.{name}.round_trip_max_abs_diff", diff)
    assert diff < 1e-5, (
        f"{name}: the tuned vector read from a BRAND NEW connection differs "
        f"from the first tuned read (max|Δ| = {diff:.6g}) — the adapter is "
        f"not being served consistently across sessions"
    )
    print(f"  {name:<6} round-trip max|Δ| = {diff:.6g}  (new connection agrees)")
print("every tower's adapter round-trips train -> save (catalog) -> serve, "
      "from a session that never trained it ✓")
```

## 4 — The corrupt-row contract, measured

`docs/guide/src/generate-image-embeddings.md`'s Error-handling table documents
three rows in ONE batch: a valid image (`_status="ok"`), a **null** image
(`_status="error"`, `"Null or missing image input"`), and a **corrupt**
image (`_status="error"`, `"Failed to decode image at row N: ..."`) — all
three landing as per-row outcomes inside a single, otherwise-successful
`infer` call. This chapter puts all three in one batch (one valid row, one
null, one genuinely undecodable) and reads back every row's own outcome,
rather than trusting the table.

```{python}
for modality, corrupt in record["corrupt_rows"].items():
    print(f"\n--- {modality} ---")
    print(f"  good row still ok:  {corrupt['good_row_still_ok']}")
    print(f"  null row:           {corrupt['null_row']}")
    print(f"  corrupt row:        {corrupt['corrupt_row']}")

    assert corrupt["good_row_still_ok"], (
        f"{modality}: a null/corrupt row in the SAME batch must not fail "
        f"the other, valid row"
    )
    assert corrupt["null_row"]["status"] == "error", corrupt["null_row"]
    assert "null" in corrupt["null_row"]["error"].lower(), corrupt["null_row"]

    # The measured fact: a corrupt (undecodable) row is a per-row
    # `_status="error"` outcome too, alongside the good row — the whole
    # `infer` call does NOT raise, and its message names the offending row.
    assert corrupt["corrupt_row"]["status"] == "error", corrupt["corrupt_row"]
    assert corrupt["corrupt_row"]["message_contains_row_index"], corrupt["corrupt_row"]
```

**The finding — a real fold-round fix, caught mid-campaign.** Earlier work on
this exact chapter measured a genuine gap: `forward_image_embedding`/
`forward_audio_embedding` called `arrow_to_images`/`arrow_to_audio` with `?`,
so a corrupt row failed the WHOLE `infer` call instead of landing as a
per-row outcome — contradicting this very doc table, which has always
described a uniform three-row contract. That measurement is cited here for
the record, not reproduced: by the time this chapter's cache was re-emitted,
`crates/jammi-ai`'s serving path had already been fixed on this same branch
(`arrow_to_images`/`arrow_to_audio` now return one `Option<Result<T>>` per
Arrow row — null -> `None`, a decode failure -> `Some(Err(..))` naming that
row, success -> `Some(Ok(..))` — so `forward_*_embedding` marks only the
failing row's status and the rest of the batch still embeds). What this
chapter measures NOW, against the shipped fix, is that the doc's three-row
contract genuinely holds: a null row and a corrupt row are BOTH per-row
`_status="error"` outcomes, on both image and audio, and neither one fails
the batch's other, valid row.

## Bridge note

> **The first real-checkpoint chapter in the fine-tuning line.** Every earlier
> `fine_tune` chapter in this book trains a small, hermetic text encoder; this
> one is the media front end's own proof, on real OpenCLIP and real CLAP
> checkpoints, through the identical public surface. The four invariants this
> chapter measures generalize past media: change-vs-base is the adapter's
> reason to exist, the same-input control is what makes that change
> interpretable rather than assumed, the round trip is what makes "saved"
> mean something a new session can observe, and the corrupt-row measurement is
> what proves a per-row contract against the branch it describes — closing,
> not merely citing, the very gap an earlier measurement on this chapter
> caught mid-campaign.
